content.title: About
content.content: Chinese broccoli (Brassica oleracea var. alboglabra), also known as gai lan, is a cruciferous vegetable. Raw Chinese broccoli has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. It is commonly used in salads, pickles, and as an ingredient in Asian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chinese broccoli differs from regular green broccoli by its lighter, almost white head and more tender florets.
In China it is called “gai lan” and has been cultivated for over 2,000 years.
It is rich in glucosinolates, which break down into compounds with anti‑cancer properties.
Raw Chinese broccoli retains more vitamins than when it is cooked.
Unlike standard broccoli, Chinese varieties are often grown in warmer climates.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Raw Chinese broccoli provides over 100 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, supporting immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene, lutein and zeaxanthin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: For some people raw broccoli can cause gas and bloating due to its raffinose content.

items.title: Possible allergies
items.content: Allergic reactions to cruciferous vegetables are rare but possible.

items.title: Interaction with medication
items.content: High vitamin K levels may affect the efficacy of anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw Chinese broccoli can be thinly sliced and added to salads, used in spring rolls, pickled, or served with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce and sesame oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a small amount of moisture. Use within 3–5 days. Discard if yellow spots or off‑odors develop.
